newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's HKMA renews contract of deputy chief.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's HKMA renews contract of deputy chief.

text.p: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) on Tuesday said it had renewed the contract of deputy chief executive David Carse for three years starting from the expiration of his current contract on April 30 next year.

Carse, responsible for banking supervision and policy issues at Hong Kong's de facto central bank, was seconded to Hong Kong from the Bank of England in 1991. As a consequence of the extension, he will be resigning from the Bank of England.

"The extension of Mr Carse's contract will ensure continuity and a smooth transition for the banking arm of the HKMA in the run-up to and beyond 1997," HKMA chief executive Joseph Yam said in a statement.
The British colony reverts to Chinese sovereignty in mid-1997. Beijing has promised to allow the HKMA to pursue an independent monetary policy beyond the handover.
